subject: Optimize toolkit — quantization & KV-cache tiering: commercial terms discussion
messages:
From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finmetrics.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finmetrics.com>, Diego Martinez <diego.m@finmetrics.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Optimize toolkit packaging and recommendations

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Diego and I discussed the Optimize toolkit capabilities and we want to understand how pricing maps to the technical recommendations you gave: specifically batching strategy, KV-cache tiering, and the quantization options you mentioned. Procurement also asked for a clear view of what discounts or credits are available for a 12–18 month pilot, and what SLAs, if any, apply to Dedicated vs Hosted.

Action items from our side: can you send a scoped commercial proposal + an engineering note that quantifies expected token savings for our workload? We run ~6M tokens/day (75% short chat queries, 25% long context retrieval), and we care about 99th percentile latency under 300ms.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Alvarez
Head of Product, FinMetrics
sofia.alvarez@finmetrics.com
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finmetrics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-05-18T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Optimize toolkit packaging and recommendations

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear signal on workload shape. I attached a short proposal (rwd_optimize_proposal_v1.pdf) and a technical appendix that Marcus compiled (see kv_cache_recommendation_diagram.png). High level:

- Pilot scope: 12 months, hosted production with optional Dedicated burst.
- Savings estimate: we expect 30–45% per-token reduction via a combined KV-cache + batching approach for your mix (Marcus' model-level sim shows ~40% on average).
- Quantization: 8-bit mixed quant works in your case with minimal quality regression; we recommend PQ4 (per-model) for embeddings-heavy routes and 4-bit for large generation-only routes.
- Packaging: three commercial paths — (A) Pay-as-you-go (no commit), (B) Pilot commit (12-mo, 60% usage coverage) + credits, (C) Dedicated minimum (monthly commit) for strict latency SLOs.

Marcus, can you add a line on latency tradeoffs in the appendix?

Next steps: I'll propose a commercial term sheet once Procurement confirms target credit size and any required SLA hours.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com
From: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finmetrics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-05-18T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Optimize toolkit packaging and recommendations

Sofia / Grace —

Quick technical detail to set expectations:

- Our measurements on a similar customer with 70/30 short/long showed a 38% token-cost improvement with prefix KV-cache + 64-token continuous batching. For FinMetrics' 6M tokens/day, that translates to roughly 2.1M tokens/day saved (ballpark).
- Latency: hosted with caching averages 85–120ms median; 99th ~260–320ms depending on model choice and traffic spikes. Dedicated pools reduce jitter — 99th drops to ~180–220ms for comparable batch sizes.
- Quantization quality: for your retrieval-heavy call patterns we recommend per-layer mixed 8-bit quant (QAT not needed). For long generative sessions, test 4-bit (q4_0) on a sample dataset; we can run a quick eval to confirm top-n accuracy delta.

I'll include a one-pager with numbers in the Drive link.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin, Solutions Architect
marcus.lin@redwood.example.com
From: Procurement <procurement@finmetrics.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finmetrics.com>, Diego Martinez <diego.m@finmetrics.com>
Date: 2028-05-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RWD-3245: term request and counterproposal

Grace —

Thanks for the materials. FinMetrics procurement is prepared to move forward on option (B) but we'd like to propose the following counterterms:

- Pilot commit: 12 months, $120k total credit up-front (recognized over the term).
- Performance credit: if 99p latency in Hosted exceeds 320ms for more than 6 hours/month, we request a service credit equal to 3% of monthly committed spend for each extra 6 hours, up to 18%.
- Discount request: 25% list discount on tokens for the pilot period, and proof of the 30–45% efficiency savings after 60 days or we revert to 10% discount.

Please confirm whether security SOC2 Type II evidence and a data-retention addendum are available within the pilot contract.

Procurement
FinMetrics
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
To: Procurement <procurement@finmetrics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, aditya_rao@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-05-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RWD-3245: term request and counterproposal

Procurement team —

Thanks — we can accommodate most of this with a few adjustments:

- Credit size: we can accept a $120k pilot credit recognized over 12 months; proposal attached (pricing_term_sheet.xlsx).
- Discount: we can offer a 20% list discount for the pilot (we're willing to split the delta if the 30–45% efficiency target isn't met at the 60-day eval). The alternative is a 15% upfront discount + an efficiency rebate structure tied to observed token savings.
- SLA credits: we are comfortable with the proposed credit structure but need to cap exposure. Proposed change: service-credit cap at 10% of monthly committed spend; escalation thresholds and remediation playbook will be in the SOW.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II evidence is available; we will attach a redacted report and a data-retention addendum (standard) as part of the Private Data Addendum.

Aditya — please confirm final language on SLA cap and provide the draft SOW. Laura, tagging you for legal redline path and signature authority thresholds.

Grace
From: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, Procurement <procurement@finmetrics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RWD-3245: term request and counterproposal

Team —

We agree to the $120k pilot credit and will bind the 20% pilot discount. SLA exposure: we will cap service-credit liability at 10% monthly committed spend and include a two-stage escalation (ops -> engineering -> exec) with defined remediation windows.

Quant/ops commitment: Redwood will run a 30-day efficiency audit starting at pilot kickoff (no charge). If the observed token savings are below 25% at the 30-day checkpoint, we will provide an additional one-time credit of 5% of the pilot total. If above 40% we will extend a 3% additional rebate on the remainder of the pilot term.

Security/support: SOC 2 Type II artifacts and the data-retention addendum are attached; Laura will follow up with the Master Services Agreement redline and signature flow.

Next: I'll publish a DocuSign with the term sheet and SOW links (see related_links). If FinMetrics agrees, sign and we'll queue an onboarding kickoff for May 28.

—Aditya Rao
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.example.com
